This approach is often preferred by developers who value the nostalgic look of old games and are willing to sacrifice some performance for the sake of aesthetics.

articles.title: My C23 Conventions
articles.summary: Modern C conventions have emerged, particularly with the introduction of C23, which has introduced several key features that have improved code quality and reduced errors. One of the most notable is the use of [[nodiscard]] to indicate that a function or variable should not be used after it is no longer needed, which has been a game-changer for fixing bugs and improving code readability. Additionally, the use of [[maybe_unused]] to indicate that a variable should not be used after it is no longer needed has been a useful pattern. These conventions have also led to the elimination of unused variables and improved code organization, making it easier to maintain and debug code.

articles.title: Two-Stack Sliding-Window Aggregation
articles.summary: A two-stack sliding-window aggregation algorithm is presented, which can be used to calculate various aggregations such as sum, length, minimum, and more. This type of aggregation is useful when a binary operator with an inverse is not available, as it can be easily implemented using a double-ended queue. The algorithm is based on the idea of two stacks, where the first stack stores the current window and the second stack stores the aggregated values. The algorithm has a time complexity of O(1) for each step, making it efficient for real-time applications.
